body:
I've seen the same issue on my machine, building a large custom codebase.

The only solution I've found is to set the --jobs option to bazel to limit the number of parallel builds that it does.

Since my machine uses about 50% RAM under nomal operating conditions, and I wanted to leave some headroom, I tried setting `--ram_utilization_factor` to a lower number (20 or 30), but doing a build still results in 100% memory usage and swapping.

From reading the documentation, it seems like bazel should be estimating the memory usage of each build command and attempting to keep the overall memory usage below this value, but this doesn't appear to work for me.

This has also shown up on stack overflow, with similar results: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/34382360/decrease-bazel-memory-usage/34399184#34399184

If it helps, the build that I'm doing is primarily large, heavily templated C++ code, where a single instance of the compiler or the linker can use multiple GB of RAM, on a machine that has 16GB of RAM.

Yes sorry for that the ressource estimation in Bazel is far from optimal and I know @philwo has been working on improving it but it's tuning some parameters. In the time being the workaround is indeed to manually set `--jobs` to limit the number of parallel jobs bazel runs.

While we have a plan for a simplified resource management system, I'm not sure if that would fix this case. The problem is that we can't reliably estimate in advance how much RAM a given action needs and also AFAIK Bazel bases its "RAM utilization factor" on the assumption that it is the only process on the system wanting to use RAM - so "80%" means "Bazel can use up to 80% of the total installed RAM" not "Bazel should make sure that the system always keeps 20% RAM free".

@damienmg is there any information I can provide you with to help fix this error? I've tried to build TensorFlow with Bazel and seem to be running into this error. I've been able to repeated a total system freeze after presumably running out of RAM 4 times now. Will update this post if the `--jobs` argument helps.

Type | Info
--- | ---
System Information | Lenovo y510p running Fedora 25 (8GB RAM, 8 cores)
Bazel | Version 0.4.5- (@non-git) installed from source
Using with | open JDK 1.8.0.121
Building command | `bazel build -c opt //tensorflow/examples/android:tensorflow_demo`

Below is an htop when my system froze (idle RAM is ~1GB):
![img_20170411_150812](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5482320/24926619/429297c6-1eca-11e7-99ae-2a4326381ee9.jpg)

@3ygun Try specifying --jobs=4. That way, Bazel should never spawn more than 4 processes in parallel. If it works fine for your system, you could put it into your ~/.bazelrc like this:

```
build --jobs=4
```

@philwo Thanks! ~~I'm trying `--jobs=20` and getting different build errors but no system freezes so 🤞 and progress?~~

Setting `--jobs=4` allowed me to complete the build however I still hit 6GB of RAM at one point while monitoring in htop. Thanks for the help!

Hi @3ygun,

would you mind trying the [ps_mem.py](https://github.com/pixelb/ps_mem) script to get an accurate memory consumption snapshot when your build hits e.g. 6 GB of RAM? It should print a list of processes sorted by their RAM consumption correctly adjusted for shared memory pages.

The output might help to figure out how we can improve the resource handling for your use case. If it's just one kind of action / program that consistently uses so much RAM, we might add a way to limit the parallelism of actions per mnemonic.

Cheers,
Philipp
@philwo Will do when I get a chance!

@philwo sorry for the delayed response but I haven't/don't know how to give you good data and believe the root of my "freezing" problem comes from some bugs in Fedora 25. This resulted from the problem coming up all to frequently and having had it completely freeze with Firefox and a terminal open...

Alas using `--jobs=1` has allowed my builds of TensorFlow to complete well multiple times. Sorry, I cannot help more.

I could try using a different command from the linked `ps_mem.py`. In the past I've just tried `sudo ps_mem` which just lists all current process RAM amounts so not useful. Is there anything specific I should try?

I filed the issue #3209 which may be a large part of my memory issue to stop spamming this one.

issue.title: Bazel process remains after build complete

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request / question:

Originally thought I was having issue #1160 however it may stem in part to Bazel seemly not deallocating/removing the process after the build is complete. Basically, this is what my `htop` looks like long after I believe my build command has/is completed: (e.g. ~1GB of still held memory)

![bazelstuff](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5482320/27258007-b0ed8bba-53bb-11e7-8b81-e55706e71cdd.png)

The [ps_mem](https://github.com/pixelb/ps_mem) program lists it as RAM held by java not bazel directly. (e.g. `963.7 MiB + 270.5 KiB = 963.9 MiB	java`)

### If possible, provide a minimal example to reproduce the problem:

I really don't know what is causing this however here is the details/process I'm using.

I'm using bazel to build TensorFlow from source to use in a Android app. The specific build command I'm using can be found [here](https://github.com/jihunhamm/Crowd-ML/blob/master/client/android/Crowd-ML/app/build.gradle#L115) and is executed by Android studio. I also independently built TensorFlow from source following the directions found [here on the TensorFlow Android example](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/tree/master/tensorflow/examples/android#building-the-demo-with-tensorflow-from-source)

The above pictured output was remains after running our app with the equivalent of:
```text
bazel build -c opt tensorflow/examples/android:tensorflow_native_libs --crosstool_top=//external:android/crosstool --cpu=<MY_CPU_TYPE> --jobs=1 --host_crosstool_top=@bazel_tools//tools/cpp:toolchain'
```

#### Why do I know the build has/is complete?

The gradle build command has finished and the app has loaded onto my phone with the app working 🌵. The screen shot and output was taken after closing Android Studio and disconnecting the phone.


### Environment info
* Operating System:

Type | Info
--- | ---
System Information | Lenovo y510p running Fedora 25 (8GB RAM, 8 cores)
Using with | open JDK 1.8.0.131

* Bazel version:

```bash
$ bazel version
Build label: 0.5.1- (@non-git)
Build target: bazel-out/local-opt/bin/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/bazel/BazelServer_deploy.jar
Build time: Mon Jun 12 22:43:46 2017 (1497307426)
Build timestamp: 1497307426
Build timestamp as int: 1497307426
```

* If `bazel info release` returns "development version" or "(@non-git)", please tell us what source tree you compiled Bazel from; git commit hash is appreciated (`git rev-parse HEAD`):
    - I downloaded the bazel source from the [releases page tag 5.1](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/releases/tag/0.5.1) using `bazel-0.5.1-dist.zip` and followed the instructions on the [bazel.build site](https://bazel.build/versions/master/docs/install-compile-source.html)
